headword: {針小棒大|しんしょうぼうだい}
gloss: making a mountain out of a molehill

definitions.gloss: making a mountain out of a molehill; exaggeration
definitions.explanation: To exaggerate a small matter into something much larger; to blow things out of proportion. Literally: making a needle (small) into a stick (large).

examples.japanese: {彼|かれ}の{話|はなし}はいつも{針小棒大|しんしょうぼうだい}だから{話半分|はなしはんぶん}に{聞|き}いておこう。
examples.english: His stories are always exaggerated, so take them with a grain of salt.

examples.japanese: マスコミは{針小棒大|しんしょうぼうだい}に{報道|ほうどう}することがある。
examples.english: The media sometimes exaggerates in their reporting.

examples.japanese: {小|ちい}さなミスを{針小棒大|しんしょうぼうだい}に{騒|さわ}ぎ{立|た}てないでほしい。
examples.english: I wish they wouldn't make such a big deal out of a small mistake.

notes:
STRUCTURE: {針|はり} (needle) + {小|しょう} (small) + {棒|ぼう} (stick/rod) + {大|だい} (large). The idiom compares a needle (something tiny) being described as a stick or rod (something much larger).

USAGE: Used as a noun or adverb (with に) to describe exaggeration or overstatement.
・{針小棒大|しんしょうぼうだい}な{話|はなし} (an exaggerated story)
・{針小棒大|しんしょうぼうだい}に{言|い}う (to exaggerate)

SIMILAR EXPRESSIONS:
・{大|おお}げさ (exaggerated, dramatic)
・{誇張|こちょう} (exaggeration)

OPPOSITE:
・{控|ひか}えめに{言|い}う (to understate)
